𝗣𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗳 𝗠𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘆 𝗟𝗮𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗔𝗰𝘁, 𝟮𝟬𝟬𝟮 (𝗣𝗠𝗟𝗔): 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝗝𝘂𝗱𝗴𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀

The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, came into force on 1 July 2005 to prevent money laundering and provide for the attachment and confiscation of property derived from criminal activities.

𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗢𝗯𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲𝘀:
• Prevent the concealment and projection of proceeds of crime as legitimate property.
• Strengthen investigation of economic offences.
• Trace, attach and confiscate proceeds of crime.
• Promote financial transparency and accountability.
𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀:
🔹 Section 3 – Offence of money laundering.
🔹 Section 4 – Punishment for money laundering.
🔹 Section 5 – Provisional attachment of property.
🔹 Section 19 – Power to arrest.
🔹 Section 24 – Burden of proof.
🔹 Section 45 – Bail provisions.

𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝗝𝘂𝗱𝗴𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀:
1. Nikesh Tarachand Shah v. Union of India
2. Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India
3. P. Chidambaram v. Directorate of Enforcement

PMLA seeks to combat financial crimes while ensuring enforcement remains consistent with constitutional rights and principles of justice.

comment: The practical challenge is balancing investigative urgency with procedural safeguards. Clear documentation of the proceeds-of-crime trail becomes critical, particularly when tracing assets through multiple legitimate transactions or third parties.
